mia: heads-up — I just pushed sparrow-embed-v2 to staging and ran the standard holdout eval with int4 quant. recall@10 is down ~4.0% vs fp16 baseline on our prod-holdout set. tagging eng-ml for triage @arjun @sophia :thinking_face:
embed-bot: automated eval results: https://ci.internal.redwood/jobs/3421 (sparrow-embed-v2 | quant=int4)
 - dataset: prod-holdout-50k
 - recall@1: 0.612 (fp16:0.635)
 - recall@5: 0.788 (fp16:0.806)
 - recall@10: 0.842 (fp16:0.878)
 - silhouette: 0.36 (fp16:0.42)
 - eval command: `rci eval embeddings --model sparrow-embed-v2 --quant int4 --dataset prod-holdout-50k --metrics recall@1,5,10,silhouette`
arjun: can you paste the exact eval command and config flags? also which quant backend (uniform/per-channel) was used?
mia: command above — used the new quant pipeline with global int4 (default uniform per-layer), per-channel was off. index built with HNSW, M=32, ef_construction=200. run took ~28m. I can rerun per-channel if we want.
sophia: first pass questions: are we comparing cosine-normalized vectors or raw dotprod? length distribution shift after quant can break dotprod. try `--normalize True` and re-evaluate. also try `--scale-by-l2` ablation.
ronit: also run a quick PCA projection before/after quant and compute centroid shifts and silhouette by label. if centroids move a lot that's a sign of additive noise from quant. per-channel quant usually helps for channel-heavy layers — try int4 per-channel and int8 per-channel and compare.
mia: running ablations now:
```bash
# reproduce baseline eval
rci eval embeddings --model sparrow-embed-v2 --quant fp16 --dataset prod-holdout-50k --metrics recall@1,5,10,silhouette --index hnsw --normalize True
# int4 uniform (what we ran)
rci eval embeddings --model sparrow-embed-v2 --quant int4 --dataset prod-holdout-50k --metrics recall@1,5,10,silhouette --index hnsw --normalize False
# int4 per-channel
rci eval embeddings --model sparrow-embed-v2 --quant int4_pc --dataset prod-holdout-50k --metrics recall@1,5,10,silhouette --index hnsw --normalize False
```
mia: quick summary from the short runs (still finishing full):
 - fp16 (normalize True): recall@10 0.878, silhouette 0.42
 - int4 uniform (normalize False): recall@10 0.842, silhouette 0.36
 - int4 per-channel (normalize False): recall@10 0.868, silhouette 0.40
so per-channel int4 recovers most of the loss. normalizing also helps a bit.
arjun: good — that suggests quant noise not model semantics. next steps: rerun int4 per-channel with `--normalize True` and also try metric L2 vs cosine (indexing/prefix differences). can you open a quick canary on staging traffic after per-channel runs? aim to compare live latency too.
sophia: add an ablation: quantize only MLP layers vs only attention to see which contributes more to centroid drift. and compute recall delta per-query-length bucket — long queries often degrade more.
ronit: also check the quant tool changelog — a recent commit toggled the zero-point handling for int4 packing; if per-layer recovered things, that might be the culprit. file an issue if you see systematic bias.
mia: will run the extra ablations and post updated numbers here. scheduling canary for tomorrow 10:00 PT if everyone is happy. tagging @eng-oncall for FYI.
